bibl.title: A new neural framework for visuospatial processing

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the cortical dorsal visual stream and what it actually comprises
span.quote: The characterization of the ventral stream as a ‘What’ pathway is relatively uncontroversial, but the nature of dorsal stream processing is less clear. Originally proposed as mediating spatial perception (‘Where’), more recent accounts suggest it primarily serves non-conscious visually guided action

span.label: whether the dorsal stream is best characterised as a Where pathway, a How pathway, or neither
span.quote: The existence of these multiple pathways, each mediating a different class of visuospatial functions, suggests that earlier characterizations of the dorsal stream as being either a perceptual Where or a motoric How pathway were insufficient to adequately capture the diversity of its visuospatial functions.

span.label: replaces the single-purpose dorsal stream with three pathways - parieto-prefrontal, parieto-premotor and parieto-medial temporal - supporting spatial working memory, visually guided action and navigation
span.quote: We review anatomical and functional evidence in primates indicating that the dorsal stream actually gives rise to three distinct, major pathways; a parieto–prefrontal pathway, a parieto–premotor pathway and a parieto–medial temporal pathway ( FIG. 1c ), which primarily support spatial working memory, visually guided action and spatial navigation, respectively.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We review anatomical and functional evidence in primates indicating that the dorsal stream actually gives rise to three distinct, major pathways; a parieto–prefrontal pathway, a parieto–premotor pathway and a parieto–medial temporal pathway ( FIG. 1c ), which primarily support spatial working memory, visually guided action and spatial navigation, respectively.

span.label: dorsal-stream visuospatial processing
span.quote: The division of cortical visual processing into distinct dorsal and ventral streams is a key framework that has guided visual neuroscience.

span.label: review
span.quote: Here, we review anatomical evidence, primarily from monkeys, in order to update the circuitry within the classical dorsal visual stream, after which we show that there is a trifurcation of this stream beyond the parietal cortex.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The three pathways acquire their different functions from their differing cortical targets rather than from their overlapping parietal sources — granular six-layered targets support perception while the agranular premotor target supports action
span.quote: To account for how these three pathways support such distinctly different visuospatial functions — conscious perception and nonconscious action — and yet emerge from overlapping sources within the posterior parietal cortex, we suggest that their differential cortical targets are largely responsible.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Regional function is generated by the region's pattern of connectivity, so densely and reciprocally connected regions necessarily share functional properties and functions blend in gradients along a pathway
span.quote: A major premise in this perspective is that the function of a region emerges from its particular pattern of connectivity, and that densely and reciprocally interconnected regions must share at least some functional properties.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The PCC and RSC sit mid-pathway and perform the conversion of egocentric parietal space codes into the allocentric codes used by the medial temporal lobe
span.quote: Consistent with its position in the parieto – medial temporal pathway, the PCC has also been proposed as an area that contributes to the translation between the egocentric representations of space in the posterior parietal cortex and the allocentric representations in the MTL (for example, REF. 119 ).

span.label: the occipito-parietal circuit is the shared antecedent from which all three pathways diverge
span.quote: This stream is now known to consist of a set of projections from early visual cortical areas to posterior regions of the parietal cortex — the latter including medial portions of the superior parietal lobule (SPL) — together with interconnections among those parietal regions.

span.label: posterior parietal representations are predominantly egocentric while medial temporal ones are mainly allocentric, with PCC and RSC coordinating between them
span.quote: The posterior parietal region seems to contain predominantly egocentric representations of space, whereas the MTL contains spatial representations of scenes that are mainly allocentric.

span.label: damage at different points along the pathway produces predictably different forms of topographic disorientation
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: a speculative anatomical account: the perception pathways target granular six-layered cortex while the action pathway targets agranular five-layered cortex
span.quote: It may not be a coincidence that the targets of the parieto – prefrontal and parieto – medial temporal (‘perception’) pathways are six-layered cortex that contain a granular lamina IV, a type of cortex that is common to all cortical sensory systems; indeed, the targets of the primary thalamocortical projection of each sensory modality contains koniocortex in lamina IV, which has the finest neuronal granulation of all.

span.label: human resting-state functional connectivity reproduces the monkey tract-tracing circuit
span.quote: Strong correlations were also observed between time courses of fMRI responses in regions that constitute the parieto–medial temporal pathway — that is, the IPL, PCC and RSC — and the parahippocampal cortex ( FIG. 3 ; see REF. 53 for similar results in monkey and see REF. 54 for related results in human connectivity).

span.label: No research directly compares the relative importance of the different functional properties within the same parietal region, so the proposed anatomical divisions are not yet functionally adjudicated.
span.quote: Unfortunately, there has been little research that directly compares the relative importance of these different functional properties (for example, peripersonal versus extrapersonal coding) within the same region.

span.label: Empirical data on the intermediate relay areas (PCC, RSC) of the proposed parieto-medial temporal pathway are sparse.
span.quote: This new framework also highlights the paucity of empirical data regarding the intermediate areas in the parieto – medial temporal pathway.

span.label: The trifurcation is not claimed to be exhaustive; further pathways may exist.
span.quote: In proposing a trifurcation in the extension of the dorsal stream, we do not mean to imply that there are three pathways only, for there may well be others.

span.label: Scope is restricted to visuospatial processing, neglecting parietal contributions to spatial processing in other modalities.
span.quote: In limiting this Review to visuospatial processing, we recognize that we have largely neglected the role that the posterior parietal cortex plays in spatial processing in other modalities.

span.label: the framework's central premise - that function follows connectivity - is stated as a premise rather than demonstrated
span.quote: A major premise in this perspective is that the function of a region emerges from its particular pattern of connectivity, and that densely and reciprocally interconnected regions must share at least some functional properties.

span.label: the area-by-area exposition is described by the authors as purely didactic, with gradients assumed instead
span.quote: In this Review, we have examined the functional properties of each area along the parieto – medial temporal pathway separately, but this approach is purely didactic. In fact, we assume that there are gradients of function within and between these areas, including their posterior parietal and medial temporal endpoints.

span.label: how the reference-frame transformations are actually performed remains unclear
span.quote: The multisynaptic projections pass through the PCC and RSC, each of which seems to contribute to the coordination of egocentric and allocentric frames of reference, although it is still unclear how these transformations between reference frames are brought about.

span.label: there may be more than three pathways; the trifurcation is not claimed to be exhaustive
span.quote: In proposing a trifurcation in the extension of the dorsal stream, we do not mean to imply that there are three pathways only, for there may well be others.

span.label: the granular versus agranular account is explicitly left for future research
span.quote: Whether or not these differences in the makeup of their cortical targets help to account for the striking differences in the functional characteristics — perception versus action — of the three pathways is a matter for future research.

span.label: navigation evidence does not exclude other visuospatial functions for the pathway
span.quote: The multisynaptic projections pass through the PCC and RSC, each of which seems to contribute to the coordination of egocentric and allocentric frames of reference, although it is still unclear how these transformations between reference frames are brought about. This pathway’s functional properties — uncovered in neuroimaging and lesion studies — clearly indicate that it is crucial for navigation, although such evidence does not exclude the possibility that it may contribute to other forms of visuospatial function as well.

span.label: the claim that the parahippocampal place area tracks layout over semantic content has published opposing views
span.quote: and is more sensitive to the spatial layout of complex scenes than to their semantic content 165 , 172 (see REFS 173 , 174 for opposing views)

span.label: the single-patient dissociation in D.F., which grounded the How account of the whole dorsal stream
span.quote: Later, a patient with agnosia (D.F.), who has a large bilateral lesion of the occipitotemporal cortex and a small left-sided lesion of the occipitoparietal cortex ( FIG. 1b ) 4 , 5 , was found to have impaired perception of objects but intact ability to reach to objects, including shaping her grasping hand to reflect the size, shape and orientation of the object.

span.label: functional connectivity in humans, used to corroborate a circuit established by tract tracing in monkeys
span.quote: Strong correlations were also observed between time courses of fMRI responses in regions that constitute the parieto–medial temporal pathway — that is, the IPL, PCC and RSC — and the parahippocampal cortex ( FIG. 3 ; see REF. 53 for similar results in monkey and see REF. 54 for related results in human connectivity).

span.label: the same anatomical stream has carried three successive names - Where, How, and now a trifurcated framework - and each name IS a functional theory rather than a label
span.quote: The characterization of the ventral stream as a ‘What’ pathway is relatively uncontroversial, but the nature of dorsal stream processing is less clear. Originally proposed as mediating spatial perception (‘Where’), more recent accounts suggest it primarily serves non-conscious visually guided action

span.label: dorsal stream is explicitly REDEFINED here: originally the pathway from striate cortex to the posterior inferior parietal lobule, now a widespread system across frontal, temporal and limbic lobes
span.quote: We conclude that the dorsal stream, which was originally defined as the pathway between the striate cortex and the posterior part of the inferior parietal lobule, actually comprises a widespread visuospatial processing system that contributes to both spatial perception and non-conscious spatial processing across numerous cortical areas in the frontal, temporal and limbic lobes.

span.label: egocentric and allocentric are the two reference frames whose transformation is the pathway's proposed job, and the mechanism of transformation is stated to be unknown
span.quote: The multisynaptic projections pass through the PCC and RSC, each of which seems to contribute to the coordination of egocentric and allocentric frames of reference, although it is still unclear how these transformations between reference frames are brought about.

span.label: topographic disorientation is not one syndrome but a family, subdivided by which part of the pathway is damaged
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: builds-on → Milner and Goodale's 'How' account of the dorsal stream
span.quote: Although this visually guided motoric contribution of the dorsal stream was also noted early 1 , the relative importance of this contribution in humans — and its characterization as a largely automatic, non-conscious process (as opposed to the conscious correlates of human perception) — were not fully appreciated until the seminal research of Milner and Goodale 4 – 6 , 8 .

span.label: contradicts → the hypothesis (from patient D.F.) that the dorsal stream serves only non-conscious action and that only the ventral stream yields conscious representations
span.quote: Notably, however, patient D.F. is capable of making conscious judgments of absolute depth 10 , which probably depend on the dorsal stream.

span.label: builds-on → Margulies and colleagues (ref. 51), human/monkey functional connectivity of medial parietal areas
span.quote: Margulies and colleagues 51 evaluated the functional (or effective) connectivity between medial parietal areas and the rest of the brain in humans and monkeys and found evidence for much of this circuitry.

span.label: contradicts → the characterisation of the dorsal stream as either a perceptual Where or a motoric How pathway
span.quote: The existence of these multiple pathways, each mediating a different class of visuospatial functions, suggests that earlier characterizations of the dorsal stream as being either a perceptual Where or a motoric How pathway were insufficient to adequately capture the diversity of its visuospatial functions.

span.label: qualifies → the claim that only the ventral stream produces representations accessible to consciousness
span.quote: Notably, however, patient D.F. is capable of making conscious judgments of absolute depth 10 , which probably depend on the dorsal stream.

span.label: extends → the original two-stream anatomy of Ungerleider and Mishkin
span.quote: The ventral stream was described as coursing through the occipitotemporal cortex to its anterior temporal target (area TE), and the dorsal stream as coursing through the occipitoparietal cortex to the posterior half of the inferior parietal lobule (area PG)

span.label: supports → the parieto-medial temporal pathway, previously not well characterised in primates
span.quote: The parieto–medial temporal pathway, which is the main focus of this paper, has not been well-characterized previously in primates (but see REFS 11 – 14 for related proposals).

span.label: dorsal stream —contrasted-with→ ventral stream
span.quote: The ventral stream was described as coursing through the occipitotemporal cortex to its anterior temporal target (area TE), and the dorsal stream as coursing through the occipitoparietal cortex to the posterior half of the inferior parietal lobule (area PG)

span.label: egocentric —contrasted-with→ allocentric
span.quote: The posterior parietal region seems to contain predominantly egocentric representations of space, whereas the MTL contains spatial representations of scenes that are mainly allocentric.

span.label: topographic disorientation —operationalised-as→ dorsal stream
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: spatial working memory —distinct-from→ visually guided action
span.quote: We review anatomical and functional evidence in primates indicating that the dorsal stream actually gives rise to three distinct, major pathways; a parieto–prefrontal pathway, a parieto–premotor pathway and a parieto–medial temporal pathway ( FIG. 1c ), which primarily support spatial working memory, visually guided action and spatial navigation, respectively.

span.label: agranular —causes→ visually guided action
span.quote: It may not be a coincidence that the targets of the parieto – prefrontal and parieto – medial temporal (‘perception’) pathways are six-layered cortex that contain a granular lamina IV, a type of cortex that is common to all cortical sensory systems; indeed, the targets of the primary thalamocortical projection of each sensory modality contains koniocortex in lamina IV, which has the finest neuronal granulation of all.

span.label: The dorsal stream is shown to trifurcate beyond parietal cortex into parieto-prefrontal, parieto-premotor and parieto-medial temporal pathways, the last running through posterior cingulate and retrosplenial cortex to the medial temporal lobe.
span.quote: Here, we identify three pathways emerging from the dorsal stream that consist of projections to the prefrontal and premotor cortices, and a major projection to the medial temporal lobe that courses both directly and indirectly through the posterior cingulate and retrosplenial cortices.

span.label: Because each of the three pathways serves a different class of visuospatial function, neither the 'Where' nor the 'How' characterisation of the dorsal stream is adequate.
span.quote: The existence of these multiple pathways, each mediating a different class of visuospatial functions, suggests that earlier characterizations of the dorsal stream as being either a perceptual Where or a motoric How pathway were insufficient to adequately capture the diversity of its visuospatial functions.

span.label: The site of damage along the parieto-medial temporal pathway predicts which specific form of topographic disorientation a patient shows.
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: Human resting-state fMRI connectivity between IPL, PCC, RSC and parahippocampal cortex converges with the monkey tract-tracing evidence for the proposed pathway.
span.quote: Strong correlations were also observed between time courses of fMRI responses in regions that constitute the parieto–medial temporal pathway — that is, the IPL, PCC and RSC — and the parahippocampal cortex ( FIG. 3 ; see REF. 53 for similar results in monkey and see REF. 54 for related results in human connectivity).

span.label: Within the inferior parietal lobule the labour is divided: only the rostral part specialises in guiding action in the space around the body, while the caudal part feeds the navigation pathway.
span.quote: Within the IPL however, only the rIPL (also known as area 7b, and composed of areas PFG and PF) is specialized for guiding action in peripersonal space.

span.label: The dorsal stream is reconceived as a widespread visuospatial system reaching frontal, temporal and limbic cortex and supporting both conscious perception and non-conscious spatial processing.
span.quote: We conclude that the dorsal stream, which was originally defined as the pathway between the striate cortex and the posterior part of the inferior parietal lobule, actually comprises a widespread visuospatial processing system that contributes to both spatial perception and non-conscious spatial processing across numerous cortical areas in the frontal, temporal and limbic lobes.

span.label: The medial temporal lobe is proposed as the site where the ventral (object) and dorsal (spatial) streams converge into a unified percept.
span.quote: Our Review suggests, as one potential answer, that a major point of convergence and perceptual integration is within the MTL, to which both the ventral stream and the parieto – medial temporal pathway project 188 .

span.label: the dorsal stream trifurcates beyond parietal cortex into prefrontal, premotor and medial temporal pathways
span.quote: We review anatomical and functional evidence in primates indicating that the dorsal stream actually gives rise to three distinct, major pathways; a parieto–prefrontal pathway, a parieto–premotor pathway and a parieto–medial temporal pathway ( FIG. 1c ), which primarily support spatial working memory, visually guided action and spatial navigation, respectively.

span.label: human resting-state connectivity reproduces the monkey anatomy of the parieto-medial temporal pathway
span.quote: Strong correlations were also observed between time courses of fMRI responses in regions that constitute the parieto–medial temporal pathway — that is, the IPL, PCC and RSC — and the parahippocampal cortex ( FIG. 3 ; see REF. 53 for similar results in monkey and see REF. 54 for related results in human connectivity).

span.label: damage at different points along the pathway yields predictably different topographic disorientations
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: landmark agnosia leaves orientation and map-making intact but destroys landmark recognition
span.quote: Patients with this type of agnosia have no difficulty in orienting themselves within an environment or in producing maps, however, they cannot recognize prominent, navigationally relevant landmarks

span.label: anterograde topographic disorientation leaves orienting intact but prevents learning new routes
span.quote: Furthermore, in keeping with its strong connections to the hippocampus, damage to the presumed human homologue of areas TF and TH leads to anterograde topographic disorientation 15 , 160 , 161 , in which patients can no longer form representations of new environments.

span.label: the parahippocampal place area responds equally to furnished and emptied rooms, tracking layout rather than content
span.quote: Finally, in line with the role of TF/TH in creating spatial representations of complex environments, the PPA responds strongly during topographic and spatial learning (for example, REFS 169 – 171 ) and is more sensitive to the spatial layout of complex scenes than to their semantic content 165 , 172 (see REFS 173 , 174 for opposing views): it shows equivalent activation in response to seeing furnished rooms containing many objects and the same rooms when emptied of all objects

span.label: patient D.F. can reach accurately for objects she cannot consciously perceive
span.quote: Later, a patient with agnosia (D.F.), who has a large bilateral lesion of the occipitotemporal cortex and a small left-sided lesion of the occipitoparietal cortex ( FIG. 1b ) 4 , 5 , was found to have impaired perception of objects but intact ability to reach to objects, including shaping her grasping hand to reflect the size, shape and orientation of the object.

span.label: but D.F. can also make conscious depth judgments that probably depend on the dorsal stream
span.quote: Notably, however, patient D.F. is capable of making conscious judgments of absolute depth 10 , which probably depend on the dorsal stream.

span.label: parieto–medial temporal pathway (one of three dorsal-stream pathways)
span.term: parieto–medial temporal pathway (one of three dorsal-stream pathways)
span.quote: We review anatomical and functional evidence in primates indicating that the dorsal stream actually gives rise to three distinct, major pathways; a parieto–prefrontal pathway, a parieto–premotor pathway and a parieto–medial temporal pathway ( FIG. 1c ), which primarily support spatial working memory, visually guided action and spatial navigation, respectively.

span.label: retrosplenial complex
span.quote: In human neuroimaging studies, a region that responds more strongly to scenes than to objects (and which overlaps both the RSC and some portions of the PCC) has been identified and labelled the retrosplenial complex 131 .

span.label: head-direction cells
span.quote: First, in both rats and monkeys, the presubicular and parasubicular targets of the projections from cIPL and RSC contain a preponderance of head-direction cells 48 , 175 , which respond selectively depending on the particular direction the animal is facing.

span.label: place cells
span.quote: Second, again in both rats and monkeys 48 , 177 , the CA1 and prosubicular targets of the projections from the cIPL and areas TF/TH ( FIG. 2b ) contain place cells, which become active whenever the animal is in, or transits through, a particular part of the environment.

span.label: allocentric spatial view cells
span.quote: In monkeys, these hippocampal subdivisions also contain allocentric spatial view cells 178 , 179 , which respond whenever the animal looks at a particular part of the environment, regardless of distance.

span.label: heading disorientation
span.quote: Specifically, RSC lesions in humans lead to heading disorientation, a form of topographic disorientation 15 , 132 in which patients are unable to orient themselves with respect to landmarks in the environment.

span.label: landmark agnosia
span.quote: Relatively little is known about the functional properties of TFO in monkeys, but damage to its likely human homologue within the lingual gyrus 131 leads to a form of topographic disorientation known as landmark agnosia 15 .

span.label: anterograde topographic disorientation
span.quote: Furthermore, in keeping with its strong connections to the hippocampus, damage to the presumed human homologue of areas TF and TH leads to anterograde topographic disorientation 15 , 160 , 161 , in which patients can no longer form representations of new environments.

span.label: cross-modal extinction
span.quote: In this disorder, patients with unilateral parietal damage will neglect a contralesional stimulus in one sensory modality when an ipsilesional stimulus is present in a different modality (for example, REF. 195 ).

span.label: parahippocampal place area (PPA)
span.quote: There is an extensive human imaging literature on the parahippocampal place area (PPA; FIG. 5c ), a region that spans the presumptive human homologues of TFO and TF/TH 164 , 165 .

span.label: dorsal stream, as originally defined
span.quote: The ventral stream was described as coursing through the occipitotemporal cortex to its anterior temporal target (area TE), and the dorsal stream as coursing through the occipitoparietal cortex to the posterior half of the inferior parietal lobule (area PG)

span.label: dorsal stream, as redefined here
span.quote: We conclude that the dorsal stream, which was originally defined as the pathway between the striate cortex and the posterior part of the inferior parietal lobule, actually comprises a widespread visuospatial processing system that contributes to both spatial perception and non-conscious spatial processing across numerous cortical areas in the frontal, temporal and limbic lobes.

span.label: the framework's central premise
span.quote: A major premise in this perspective is that the function of a region emerges from its particular pattern of connectivity, and that densely and reciprocally interconnected regions must share at least some functional properties.

span.label: three pathways, not claimed to be exhaustive — the proposed trifurcation, with the authors noting there may well be others
span.quote: In proposing a trifurcation in the extension of the dorsal stream, we do not mean to imply that there are three pathways only, for there may well be others.

span.label: location of damage along the pathway
span.term: location of damage along the pathway
span.quote: In addition, we show that damage to the parieto–medial temporal pathway in humans results in various forms of topographic disorientation 15 that differ predictably depending on where along the pathway the damage has occurred.

span.label: egocentric versus allocentric reference frame
span.quote: The posterior parietal region seems to contain predominantly egocentric representations of space, whereas the MTL contains spatial representations of scenes that are mainly allocentric.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1038/nrn3008.
